Thus, 𝖽𝗂𝗇𝗏2⁡(dv)=𝗍𝗉⁡(y)−δy,0\dinv_{2}(d_{v})=\tp(y)-\delta_{y,0} remains valid for dv∈Vg​(T)d_{v}\in V_{g}(T).

We are now ready to prove Proposition 4.4.

where dv′d^{\prime}_{v} is the shuffle of dvd_{v}.

∑dv∈Vg​(T^o)𝖽𝗂𝗇𝗏1⁡(dv)+(n2)=∑x∈Me​(T^o)(𝗍𝗉⁡(x)−1)=∑dv′𝖽𝗂𝗇𝗏2⁡(dv′),\sum_{d_{v}\in V_{g}(\hat{T}_{o})}\dinv_{1}(d_{v})+\binom{n}{2}=\sum_{x\in M_{e}(\hat{T}_{o})}(\tp(x)-1)=\sum_{d^{\prime}_{v}}\dinv_{2}(d^{\prime}_{v}), (49)

4.4 Proof of Theorem 1.3

We remind the reader from (3) and (4) that the polynomial ADn⁡(z,q,t)\AD_{n}(z;q,t) is the generating polynomial of domino tilings of RλR_{\lambda}, where λ=(nn)\lambda=(n^{n}).

ADn⁡(z,q,t)=∑T∈𝒯⁡(Rλ)z𝖽𝗂𝖺𝗀𝗌⁡(T)​q𝖺𝗋𝖾𝖺⁡(T)​t𝖽𝗂𝗇𝗏⁡(T).\AD_{n}(z;q,t)=\sum_{T\in\T\left(R_{\lambda}\right)}z^{\diags(T)}q^{\area(T)}t^{\dinv(T)}. (51)

For a subset 𝒟\mathcal{D} of 𝒯⁡(Rλ)\T(R_{\lambda}), we define the generating polynomial of domino tilings of 𝒟\mathcal{D} by

ADn⁡(𝒟,z,q,t)=∑T∈𝒟z𝖽𝗂𝖺𝗀𝗌⁡(T)​q𝖺𝗋𝖾𝖺⁡(T)​t𝖽𝗂𝗇𝗏⁡(T).\AD_{n}(\mathcal{D};z;q,t)=\sum_{T\in\mathcal{D}}z^{\diags(T)}q^{\area(T)}t^{\dinv(T)}. (52)

We first discuss the impact of changing the orientation of dominoes—–either from two horizontal to two vertical dominoes or vice versa—–in each odd or even block on our three statistics 𝖽𝗂𝖺𝗀𝗌\diags, 𝖺𝗋𝖾𝖺\area, and 𝖽𝗂𝗇𝗏\dinv. In each odd block of T^o\hat{T}_{o}, we observe that changing two horizontal dominoes to two vertical dominoes decreases 𝖺𝗋𝖾𝖺⁡(T^o)\area(\hat{T}_{o}) by 11 and 𝖽𝗂𝖺𝗀𝗌⁡(T^o)\diags(\hat{T}_{o}) by 11. Thus, changing the orientation of dominoes in each odd block of T^o\hat{T}_{o} preserves 𝖺𝗋𝖾𝖺⁡(T^o)−𝖽𝗂𝖺𝗀𝗌⁡(T^o)\area(\hat{T}_{o})-\diags(\hat{T}_{o}). For a vertical domino dv∈V⁡(To^)d_{v}\in V(\hat{T_{o}}), it is not hard to see that changing two horizontal dominoes to two vertical dominoes in each odd block of T^o\hat{T}_{o} keeps the number of domino pairs involving dvd_{v} unchanged (viewing dvd_{v} as the type I reference domino). This implies that changing the orientation of dominoes in each odd block preserves 𝖽𝗂𝗇𝗏1⁡(dv)\dinv_{1}(d_{v}).

Let T~o\widetilde{T}_{o} be the set consisting of domino tilings obtained from ToT_{o} by filling the odd blocks of ToT_{o} with either two horizontal or two vertical dominoes. Note that T^o\hat{T}_{o} is one of the elements of T~o\widetilde{T}_{o} and |T~o|=2m|\widetilde{T}_{o}|=2^{m}. The total weight of T~o\widetilde{T}_{o} can be obtained as follows. Starting with the odd-deficient tiling ToT_{o}, we sequentially fill the iith odd block with dominoes for i=1,2,…,mi=1,2,\dots,m (the order of filling does not matter). If the iith odd block is filled by two horizontal dominoes, 𝖽𝗂𝖺𝗀𝗌⁡(To)\diags(T_{o}) increases by 11 while 𝖺𝗋𝖾𝖺⁡(To)\area(T_{o}) and 𝖽𝗂𝗇𝗏⁡(To)\dinv(T_{o}) remain unchanged (due to the way we define them (29) and (40)). This contributes a factor of zz to the weight. On the other hand, if the iith odd block is filled by two vertical dominoes, 𝖽𝗂𝖺𝗀𝗌⁡(To)\diags(T_{o}) remains the same, 𝖺𝗋𝖾𝖺⁡(To)\area(T_{o}) decreases by 11 and we assume 𝖽𝗂𝗇𝗏⁡(To)\dinv(T_{o}) increases by ki=𝖽𝗂𝗇𝗏1⁡(di)k_{i}=\dinv_{1}(d_{i}), where did_{i} is one of the vertical dominoes filled, with its bottom unit square colored black. This follows from the discussion in the previous paragraph. This adds a factor of q−1​tkiq^{-1}t^{k_{i}} to the weight.

In total, filling the iith odd block contributes a factor of z+q−1​tkiz+q^{-1}t^{k_{i}} to the weight. Therefore, the total weight of T~o\widetilde{T}_{o} is given by

ADn⁡(T~o,z,q,t)=z𝖽𝗂𝖺𝗀𝗌⁡(To)​q𝖺𝗋𝖾𝖺⁡(To)​t𝖽𝗂𝗇𝗏⁡(To)​∏i=1m(z+q−1​tki).\AD_{n}(\widetilde{T}_{o};z;q,t)=z^{\diags(T_{o})}q^{\area(T_{o})}t^{\dinv(T_{o})}\prod_{i=1}^{m}(z+q^{-1}t^{k_{i}}). (53)

Summing over all odd-deficient tilings in (53) gives the generating polynomial of domino tilings of the extended ADn\AD_{n}.

ADn⁡(z,q,t)=∑ToADn⁡(T~o,z,q,t).\AD_{n}(z;q,t)=\sum_{T_{o}}\AD_{n}(\widetilde{T}_{o};z;q,t). (54)

In each even block of T^e\hat{T}_{e}, we observe that changing two horizontal dominoes to two vertical dominoes decreases 𝖽𝗂𝖺𝗀𝗌⁡(T^e)\diags(\hat{T}_{e}) by 11 but 𝖺𝗋𝖾𝖺⁡(T^e)\area(\hat{T}_{e}) remains unchanged. For a vertical domino dv′∈V⁡(Te^)d^{\prime}_{v}\in V(\hat{T_{e}}), it is not hard to see that changing the orientation of dominoes in each even block of T^e\hat{T}_{e} keeps the number of domino pairs involving dv′d^{\prime}_{v} unchanged (viewing dv′d^{\prime}_{v} as the type II reference domino). Thus, 𝖽𝗂𝗇𝗏2⁡(dv′)\dinv_{2}(d^{\prime}_{v}) is preserved.

Let T~e\widetilde{T}_{e} be the set consisting of domino tilings obtained from Te=S⁡(To)T_{e}=S(T_{o}) by filling the even blocks of TeT_{e} with either two horizontal or two vertical dominoes. Note that T^e\hat{T}_{e} is one of the elements of T~e\widetilde{T}_{e} and |T~e|=2m+n+1|\widetilde{T}_{e}|=2^{m+n+1}. The total weight of T~e\widetilde{T}_{e} can be obtained similarly. Starting with the even-deficient tiling TeT_{e}, we sequentially fill the iith even block with dominoes for i=1,2,…,m+n+1i=1,2,\dots,m+n+1 (the order of filling does not matter). If the iith even block is filled by two horizontal dominoes, 𝖽𝗂𝖺𝗀𝗌⁡(Te)\diags(T_{e}) increases by 11 while 𝖺𝗋𝖾𝖺⁡(Te)\area(T_{e}) and 𝖽𝗂𝗇𝗏⁡(Te)\dinv(T_{e}) remain unchanged (due to (30) and (40)). This contributes a factor of zz to the weight. On the other hand, if the iith even block is filled by two vertical dominoes, 𝖽𝗂𝖺𝗀𝗌⁡(Te)\diags(T_{e}) and 𝖺𝗋𝖾𝖺⁡(Te)\area(T_{e}) remain the same, and we assume 𝖽𝗂𝗇𝗏⁡(Te)\dinv(T_{e}) increases by ℓi=𝖽𝗂𝗇𝗏2⁡(di′)\ell_{i}=\dinv_{2}(d^{\prime}_{i}), where di′d^{\prime}_{i} is one of the vertical dominoes filled, with its bottom unit square colored black. This follows from the discussion in the previous paragraph and adds a factor of tℓit^{\ell_{i}} to the weight.

In total, filling the iith even block contributes a factor of z+tℓiz+t^{\ell_{i}} to the weight. Therefore, the total weight of T~e\widetilde{T}_{e} is given by

ADn+1⁡(T~e,z,q,t)=z𝖽𝗂𝖺𝗀𝗌⁡(Te)​q𝖺𝗋𝖾𝖺⁡(Te)​t𝖽𝗂𝗇𝗏⁡(Te)​∏i=1m+n+1(z+tℓi).\AD_{n+1}(\widetilde{T}_{e};z;q,t)=z^{\diags(T_{e})}q^{\area(T_{e})}t^{\dinv(T_{e})}\prod_{i=1}^{m+n+1}(z+t^{\ell_{i}}). (55)

Summing over all even-deficient tilings in (55) gives the generating polynomial of domino tilings of the extended ADn+1\AD_{n+1}.

ADn+1⁡(z,q,t)=∑TeADn+1⁡(T~e,z,q,t).\AD_{n+1}(z;q,t)=\sum_{T_{e}}\AD_{n+1}(\widetilde{T}_{e};z;q,t). (56)

In the following lemma, we show how the dinv statistic of the vertical dominoes contained in each odd or even block changes under the domino shuffling. This result will be used later to prove Theorem 1.3.

Lemma 4.8.

Let TT be a domino tiling of the extended ADn\AD_{n} with mm odd blocks. Suppose the odd blocks of ToT_{o} and the even blocks of Te=S⁡(To)T_{e}=S(T_{o}) are filled with two vertical dominoes. Let did_{i} (resp., dj′d^{\prime}_{j}) be the vertical domino with its bottom unit square colored black contained in the iith odd block (resp., the jjth even block), for each i=1,…,mi=1,\dots,m (resp., j=1,…,m+n+1j=1,\dots,m+n+1). Assuming 𝖽𝗂𝗇𝗏1⁡(di)=ki\dinv_{1}(d_{i})=k_{i} and 𝖽𝗂𝗇𝗏2⁡(dj′)=ℓj\dinv_{2}(d^{\prime}_{j})=\ell_{j}, then as multisets,

{ℓ1,ℓ2,…,ℓm+n+1}∖{k1,k2,…,km}={0,1,…,n}.\{\ell_{1},\ell_{2},\dotsc,\ell_{m+n+1}\}\setminus\{k_{1},k_{2},\dotsc,k_{m}\}=\{0,1,\dotsc,n\}. (57)
Proof.

Let Me​(T)M_{e}(T) be the extended ASM of TT. Define the reading word of TT by recording the non-zero entries of Me​(T)M_{e}(T) from top to bottom and right to left. We write w(T)=w1w2⋯wpw(T)=w_{1}w_{2}\cdots w_{p} with wi∈{−1,1}w_{i}\in\{-1,1\} for the reading word of TT and set 𝗍𝗉⁡(wi)=∑s=1i−1ws\tp(w_{i})=\sum_{s=1}^{i-1}w_{s} to be the top partial sum (Section 4.3) of wiw_{i} in Me​(T)M_{e}(T). By Lemma 4.6,

ki\displaystyle k_{i} =𝖽𝗂𝗇𝗏1⁡(di)=𝗍𝗉⁡(wai)−1=∑s=1ai−1ws−1,\displaystyle=\dinv_{1}(d_{i})=\tp(w_{a_{i}})-1=\sum_{s=1}^{a_{i}-1}w_{s}-1,
ℓj\displaystyle\ell_{j} =𝖽𝗂𝗇𝗏2⁡(dj′)=𝗍𝗉⁡(wbj)=∑s=1bj−1ws,\displaystyle=\dinv_{2}(d^{\prime}_{j})=\tp(w_{b_{j}})=\sum_{s=1}^{b_{j}-1}w_{s},

where wai=−1w_{a_{i}}=-1 and wbj=1w_{b_{j}}=1 for some positive integers aia_{i} and bjb_{j}.

Next, we find (1,−1)(1,-1) pairs from the reading word w⁡(T)w(T) as follows. From left to right, for each −1-1 in w⁡(T)w(T), find the nearest unpaired 11 on its left, and form a (1,−1)(1,-1) pair. For example, the reading word of the extended ASM given in Figure 12 is w=1,1,−1,1,1,1w=1,1,-1,1,1,1 and (w2,w3)(w_{2},w_{3}) forms the only (1,−1)(1,-1) pair. Since we assume TT has mm odd blocks, the reading word w⁡(T)w(T) contains mm −1-1’s, resulting in mm (1,−1)(1,-1) pairs. If wb0=1w_{b_{0}}=1 is paired with wa0=−1w_{a_{0}}=-1 (b0<a0)(b_{0}<a_{0}) in the reading word w⁡(T)w(T), then we have the same number of 11’s and −1-1’s in between wb0w_{b_{0}} and wa0w_{a_{0}}. This implies that

𝗍𝗉⁡(wa0)−1=∑s=1a0−1ws−wb0=∑s=1b0−1ws=𝗍𝗉⁡(wb0).\tp(w_{a_{0}})-1=\sum_{s=1}^{a_{0}-1}w_{s}-w_{b_{0}}=\sum_{s=1}^{b_{0}-1}w_{s}=\tp(w_{b_{0}}). (58)

Thus, the associated vertical dominoes contribute the same number of domino pairs, that is, ka0=𝖽𝗂𝗇𝗏1⁡(da0)=𝖽𝗂𝗇𝗏2⁡(db0′)=ℓb0k_{a_{0}}=\dinv_{1}(d_{a_{0}})=\dinv_{2}(d^{\prime}_{b_{0}})=\ell_{b_{0}}. This implies that these dinv contributions cancel out on the left-hand side of (57), it remains to show that the dinv contribution from those unpaired 11’s in the reading word w⁡(T)w(T) is given by {0,1,…,n}\{0,1,\dots,n\}.

For each unpaired wbj=1w_{b_{j}}=1 in the reading word w⁡(T)w(T), it is easy to see that

𝖽𝗂𝗇𝗏2⁡(dbj′)=𝗍𝗉⁡(wbj)=∑s=1bj−1ws=j−1,\dinv_{2}(d^{\prime}_{b_{j}})=\tp(w_{b_{j}})=\sum_{s=1}^{b_{j}-1}w_{s}=j-1, (59)

for j=1,2,…,n+1j=1,2,\dotsc,n+1. In other words, the left-hand side of (57) is given by {0,1,…,n}\{0,1,\dotsc,n\}, as desired. ∎

Recall that Theorem 1.3 states that the polynomial ADn⁡(z,q,t)\AD_{n}(z;q,t) is given by the product formula. We close this section with the proof of Theorem 1.3.

Proof of Theorem 1.3.

We prove it by induction on nn. For the base case n=1n=1, the extended AD1\AD_{1} is a 2×22\times 2 square which has two domino tilings: the tiling with two horizontal dominoes is weighted by zz while the tiling with two vertical dominoes is weighted by 11. Thus, AD1⁡(z,q,t)=z+1\AD_{1}(z;q,t)=z+1 matches (5) when n=1n=1.

Now, we assume the statement holds for nn. Substituting z​q−1zq^{-1} for zz in (53) yields

5 An Open Problem

In this section, we formulate a conjecture regarding the polynomials Pλ​(z,q,t)P_{\lambda}(z;q,t) (see (3)).

In Theorem 1.3, we prove that the polynomial Pλ​(z,q,t)P_{\lambda}(z;q,t) factors nicely when λ=(nn)\lambda=(n^{n}). Based on computations for small partitions, Pλ​(z,q,t)P_{\lambda}(z;q,t) appear to have many factors of the form (z+qi​tj)(z+q^{i}t^{j}). We conjecture that these linear factors are determined by the rank of the partition λ\lambda, that is, the size of the Durfee square contained in λ\lambda ([18, Page 289]). We have verified it for all partitions of size at most 99.

Conjecture 5.1.

For any partition λ\lambda of rank rr, then the polynoimal Pλ​(z,q,t)P_{\lambda}(z;q,t) is divisible by linear factors (z+qi​tj)(z+q^{i}t^{j}) for i,j≥0i,j\geq 0 and i+j<ri+j<r,

Pλ​(z,q,t)=Qλ​(z,q,t)⋅∏i,j≥0​ and ​i+j<r(z+qi​tj),P_{\lambda}(z;q,t)=Q_{\lambda}(z;q,t)\cdot\prod_{i,j\geq 0\text{ and }i+j<r}(z+q^{i}t^{j}), (63)

where the quotient Qλ​(z,q,t)Q_{\lambda}(z;q,t) is a polynomial in ℤ≥0​[z,q,t]\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}[z,q,t].

Theorem 1.3 directly confirms that Conjecture 5.1 holds for λ=(nn)\lambda=(n^{n}), where λ\lambda is equal to its Durfee square. In general, the rank of λ\lambda is equal to the number of nonzero border strip lengths n0,n1,…,nkn_{0},n_{1},\dots,n_{k}, and therefore the number of nontrivial paths in a λ\lambda-family of Schröder paths. It would be an interesting problem to prove Conjecture 5.1 either through the combinatorics of domino shuffling or using symmetric functions and Macdonald polynomials via Theorem 1.1.
